Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We propose a substantial, readily administered settlement that delivers relief directly to the identified class and ensures any fee reduction benefits class members rather than Brightline. This is an opening proposal; we are prepared to discuss resolution promptly.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Brightline is prepared to resolve the nationwide claims with direct payments to identified members, but your opening proposal exceeds our authorized total. This is a serious counterproposal for prompt resolution.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate the commitment to automatic payments and the proposed fee protections. To resolve the case promptly, we counter with a $35 million class fund and $9 million in attorneys’ fees, retaining the other terms: clear sailing, any unawarded fees reverting to the class, and automatic distribution.

Whitcombe Reyes LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Whitcombe Reyes LLP.message: Given the scale of the alleged renewal charges, the strength of the surviving claims, and Brightline’s ability to distribute payments directly to identified members, our opening proposal is a $40 million class fund with automatic distribution and $8 million in attorneys’ fees and expenses. Brightline would agree not to oppose the fee request, and any amount the court declines to award would be added to the class fund. This proposal is intended to resolve the claims of the entire class.

Whitcombe Reyes LLP.speaker: defense
Whitcombe Reyes LLP.message: We appreciate the automatic-distribution structure and the proposal to have any fee reduction benefit the class. Brightline cannot meet the proposed total, but offers the following substantial counterproposal to settle all class claims.

Whitcombe Reyes LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Whitcombe Reyes LLP.message: We appreciate Brightline’s substantial counterproposal and its agreement to automatic payments and to have any court-reduced fee benefit the class. To reflect the scale of the charges and resolve the claims for the entire class, we propose increasing the class fund to $35 million while keeping the fee and remaining terms unchanged. This is a meaningful move toward resolution.

Ostrander Bell LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Ostrander Bell LLP.message: The class is readily identifiable, so a settlement should deliver relief directly rather than depend on claims participation. Our opening proposal is $35 million for the class, distributed automatically, plus $10 million in attorneys’ fees and expenses. Brightline would not oppose the fee request, and any amount the court does not award would go to the class.

Ostrander Bell LLP.speaker: defense
Ostrander Bell LLP.message: Brightline values direct relief to the identified class and is making a substantial counterproposal to resolve the overlapping litigation. The total must remain within our authorization.

Ostrander Bell LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Ostrander Bell LLP.message: Ostrander Bell accepts Brightline’s latest term sheet as binding, subject to court approval.

private_notes.private_reasoning: Anchor high while emphasizing automatic distribution and protecting class members if the court reduces fees. The class’s expected trial recovery is substantial, though certification risk and delay support settlement. A strong opening also accounts for competing counsel seeking the first approved settlement.

Open with a strong but supportable demand reflecting the substantial classwide exposure and the value of automatic distribution, while preserving room to negotiate. Request a meaningful fee that accounts for the firm's investment, with any fee the court declines to award benefiting the class.

Open with a substantial, distribution-focused proposal reflecting the class’s scale and the value of automatic payment, while seeking a separate fee award that compensates counsel and places court-disallowed fees with the class.

Do not accept any above-cap opening term sheet. Counter with automatic distribution, clear sailing, and fee reductions benefiting the class, while keeping total cash outlay below the $40 million authorization. Use differentiated offers to test which counsel can resolve the matter most efficiently.

The defense offer provides substantial automatic relief and a meaningful fee, but there is room to improve it. Given the litigation and certification risks, I should make a credible counter that preserves direct distribution and the class-benefiting treatment of any fee reduction, while moving materially toward settlement.

The defense offer provides a substantial, automatic recovery for the class and a meaningful fee, but there is room to seek a higher class fund. A moderate counter keeps negotiations moving while preserving the important automatic-distribution and fee-reversion terms.

The latest offer provides $29 million in automatic class payments and $7 million in fees and expenses, with any unawarded fee going to the class. Given the meaningful certification and trial risks and the competing overlapping actions, securing this substantial direct relief now is preferable to risking the settlement opportunity for a modest increase.

declaration.negotiation_history_statement: The settlement was reached through arm’s-length negotiations between class counsel and Brightline’s counsel. The parties exchanged complete settlement proposals addressing class relief and attorneys’ fees together; they did not first agree on class relief and only later discuss fees. Class counsel accepted Brightline’s complete proposal, subject to court approval. Consistent with the confidentiality of the negotiations, this statement does not disclose the parties’ specific offers or other mediation communications.
